question.text: If USDINR spot is 83.50, India's 3-month rate is 6.5% p.a., and US 3-month rate is 4.5% p.a., what is the approximate 3-month futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the period-adjusted interest-rate-parity formula (pp. 62-63): F = 83.50 x (1 + 0.065 x 0.25) / (1 + 0.045 x 0.25) = 83.50 x 1.01625 / 1.01125 = approximately 83.91, which rounds to the nearest option 83.92. The Trap: Use 0.25 for 3 months (3/12). Annual rates must be adjusted for the holding period before applying IRP. Note: Period-adjusted IRP pricing is covered in the Series I workbook. The 3-month forward premium of about 42 paise is much less than the annual interest-rate differential because you only carry the position for a quarter.
